newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE SHARES END WEEK UP, BUT SEEN COMING OFF.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE SHARES END WEEK UP, BUT SEEN COMING OFF.

text.p: Zimbabwe's industrial index closed firmer on Friday, riding on gains in some heavy-weight shares, but brokers said fundamentals still pointed to a weak perfomance in coming weeks.
"The market was up on the back of gains in some of the heavies but we think this will be shortlived. (Investor) sentiment still remains negative," commented one.

The brokers say steadily rising interest rates are proving the undoing of the bourse by luring investors to the local money market. They say the stocks can only start recovering after government unveils its annual budget in July, and only if the budget promises reduced government spending, and hence lower inflation and interest rates.
On Friday the key index added 35.40 points to close at 10,062.31, gaining 46.99 points on the week.

Counters to advance included wood and glass product makers PGI and bankers Barclays , which both went up 50 cents to 450 and 3,000 respectively, while cement firm Circem at 480 and agricultural investors Chemco at 4,050 each gained 30 cents.

Others to trade firmer were hotel giant Meikles , window and door manufacturer Radar and winer makers Cairns , all up 25 cents to 2,625, 400 and 1,375 respectively. Clothing retailer Edgars finished off the winners' list, firming by 20 cents to 695.
In minings, most counters traded unchanged from previous levels with the seven-share index there losing 4.61 points, though it gained a marginal 0.94 points on the week.
